To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed procedure for analyzing a variance-stabilized simulation metamodel provides better confidence-interval performance than the conventional approach, (ii) the conventional approach can be used as a valid approximation to the proposed procedure when the variance-stabilizing transformations are applied to the simulation output, and (iii) the conventional approach should not be used when the variance-stablizing transformations are applied only to the simulation inputs

(i) the delta method can be used to compute a valid confidence bound for a metamodel-based estimator of the expected value of an untransformed response and (ii) this confidence bound can be used in an approximate t-test to compare the metamodel-based estimator to an estimator obtained from running the simulation at a selected factor level combination.
the proposed technique for analyzing a transformed-based simulation metodel is more effective than a conventional technique at maintaining confidence-interval coverage over a wide range.

the variance-stabilizing transformations used in simulation metamodeling should be treated as a means for improving the statistical efficiency of the resulting metamodels and not as an alternative to the more standard techniques for metamodel analysis.
